newsitem.title: CANADA: Novagas has enough support for gas liquids plant.
newsitem.headline: Novagas has enough support for gas liquids plant.

text.p: NOVA Corp unit Novagas Clearinghouse Ltd said on Friday it had enough signed agrements from natural gas shippers to build a C$40 million deep cut processing plant near Taylor, British Columbia.
Novagas said the plant was projected to produce 12,000 barrels per day of natural gas liquids.

"We're advancing our engineering design for the Taylor plant and we intend to file our regulatory applications with B.C. government authorities by mid-February," Randy Findlay, executive vice-president of Novagas, said in a statement.
"The Taylor plant is the key to NCL's integrated liquids strategy, including a gathering system and a liquids fractionator."

Novagas unveiled a plan in May to build and operate a natural gas liquids gathering system in northeastern B.C. and northwestern Alberta and a fractionation facility at Redwater, 30 kilometres northwest of Edmonton.
It said industry support for the Taylor plant provided the "critical impetus" for the facilities to be built.
Novagas said its gathering system would carry liquids produced at Taylor to an existing storage facility at Redwater.
The gathering system would also collect additional gas liquids from other processing facilities en route, it said.
At Redwater, Novagas intends to build a C$100 million fractionation facility to process 65,000 barrels of gas liquids per day.

The Taylor plant, the liquids gathering system and the Redwater fractionation facility could be operational by April 1998, pending regulatory approvals, the company said. ((-- Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
